question.text: Scenario: Sunrise Mutual Fund operates an equity scheme called Sunrise Growth Fund and a liquid scheme called Sunrise Cash Fund. The following events occur during a particular week: Monday: Portfolio value of Sunrise Growth Fund is Rs.800 crore with liabilities of Rs.20 crore and 40 crore units outstanding. Mr. Amit Kumar submits a purchase application for the Growth Fund at 2:45 PM with Rs.5 lakh via RTGS (credited same day). Mrs. Rekha Joshi submits a purchase application for the Cash Fund (liquid) at 1:15 PM with Rs.10 lakh via RTGS (credited same day). Tuesday: The Growth Fund's portfolio rises to Rs.820 crore (same liabilities and units outstanding as Monday for simplicity). Mr. Vikash Patel submits a redemption request for 10,000 units of the Growth Fund at 3:20 PM. Wednesday: The Growth Fund's portfolio value is Rs.810 crore. Mr. Vikash's redemption is processed using the applicable NAV. The Growth Fund's closing NAV on Friday of the previous week was Rs.19.40. All days mentioned are business days. Question 3 of 5: Mrs. Rekha Joshi's liquid fund purchase was submitted at 1:15 PM on Monday with RTGS credited the same day. What NAV applies to her purchase?

answer.text: Monday's closing NAV since RTGS was credited on Monday
Tuesday's closing NAV as the next business day
Friday's closing NAV of the previous week
Sunday's closing NAV — the closing NAV of the day immediately preceding the day of receipt of the application, since liquid funds calculate NAV for each calendar day

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series II-B workbook (pp.142, 144-145), for liquid and overnight fund purchases received before the 1:30 PM cut-off with funds available for utilisation before the cut-off, the applicable NAV is the closing NAV of the day immediately preceding the day of receipt of the application. Liquid funds calculate NAV for each calendar day (not only business days). Since Rekha applied on Monday before 1:30 PM with funds credited Monday, Sunday's closing NAV applies. The Trap: Unlike equity funds, liquid funds use the PREVIOUS calendar day's NAV — not the same day's NAV. And because liquid-fund NAVs are computed every calendar day, the "previous day" is Sunday, not the previous business day (Friday). This anti-arbitrage rule prevents investors from buying at a known NAV. Note: For corporate treasury clients managing overnight cash, explain that Monday liquid-fund purchases funded before 1:30 PM get Sunday's NAV (not Friday's), because liquid funds compute NAV for every calendar day including weekends.
